answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a real tidal gauge on a summit reservoir ringed by willow trees, calibrated in person by an independent hydrologist and logged publicly. Random checks summon the holder to read that gauge live within minutes, and one operator cannot staff two reservoirs at once. The gauge fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real gauge, another reservoir visit, another human, and twice the prior fee, while the tide itself sets an un-rushable schedule.
